4.3.1.10.2 Queueing for ‘event’ Reception
In case the swImplPolicy is set to queued the received ‘events’ have to be buffered
in a queue.
Note: A loss of events might occur in inter-ECU communication even if the receiver
queue length is sufficient. The timing of the system has to be set up in a way that it is
ensured that the COM stack on the sender side is processed before the next event is
written by the sender.
[SWS_Rte_02521]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107
⌈The RTE shall implement a receive queue for each event-like data element (swIm-
plPolicy = queued) of a receive port.⌋
[SWS_Rte_08940] Queue length for the receiver side
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00110
⌈The RTE shall determine the queue length for the receiver side according to the fol-
lowing priority rules (upmost in the list goes first):
1. value of the ECU-C parameter RteQueuedReceiverQueueLength
2. value of the queueLength attribute of the QueuedReceiverComSpec
⌋
[SWS_Rte_02522]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107, SRS_Rte_00110
⌈The events shall be written to the end of the queue and read (consuming) from the
front of the queue (i.e. the queue is first-in-first-out).⌋
[SWS_Rte_02523]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107, SRS_Rte_00110
⌈If a new event is received when the queue is already filled, the RTE shall discard the
received event and set an error flag.⌋
[SWS_Rte_02524]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107, SRS_Rte_00110, SRS_Rte_00094
⌈The error flag described in [SWS_Rte_02523] shall be reset during the next explicit
read access on the queue. In this case, the status value RTE_E_LOST_DATA shall be
presented to the application together with the data.⌋
[SWS_Rte_08621] Transformers not executed when queue is empty and execut-
eDespiteDataUnavailability is disabled
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00247
